en: all of a sudden; all at once; impulsively

examples.en: The child ran over and threw its arms around its mom.
As soon as I saw my friend, tears burst out.

examples.ko: 갑자기 와락 겁이 나서 뒤를 돌아봤어요.
examples.en: Suddenly I got scared all at once and looked behind me.

examples.ko: 그 사람이 내 손을 와락 잡았어요.
examples.en: He grabbed my hand all of a sudden.
The feeling of missing them rushed over me.
My younger sibling lunged at me suddenly and I was startled.

explain: 갑자기 힘 있게 움직이거나 감정이 확 올라올 때 써요. '안다', '잡다', '달려들다', '쏟아지다'와 자주 같이 나와요. 눈물이나 감정에는 '왈칵'도 써요.

phrases.en: I hugged my friend tightly when we met after a long time.
phrases.nuance_ko: 표제어와 함께 가장 자주 쓰이는 짝말로, 갑자기 힘 있게 안는 모습이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common pairing, describing a sudden, forceful hug.

phrases.en: The puppy suddenly jumped at me and I was startled.
phrases.nuance_ko: 갑자기 힘 있게 움직이는 동작에 써서 놀라운 느낌을 줘요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for a sudden, forceful movement that gives a startled feeling.

phrases.example: 엄마 목소리를 듣자 눈물이 왈칵 났어요.
phrases.en: When I heard my mom's voice, tears welled up all at once.
phrases.nuance_ko: 비슷한 말로, 눈물이나 감정이 한꺼번에 올라올 때 특히 잘 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A similar word, especially good when tears or emotions surge up at once.

explain_en: Sudden rush or embrace, or feeling surging, not anger. It is used for a sudden, forceful movement or a surge of emotion. It often appears with '안다', '잡다', '달려들다', and '쏟아지다'. For tears or feelings, '왈칵' is also used.

t90.ax: He grabbed my hand all of a sudden.

en: this and that; saying one thing and another

examples.en: Don't go saying this and that about other people's business.
Stop making excuses and apologize first.

examples.ko: 사람들이 우리 사이를 두고 이러쿵저러쿵 말이 많아요.
examples.en: People have a lot to say about the two of us.

examples.ko: 이러쿵저러쿵 따지다 보니 약속 시간에 늦었어요.
examples.en: We argued back and forth, and I ended up late for the appointment.
The neighbors keep spreading rumors about this and that.

examples.ko: 이러쿵저러쿵 설명을 들었지만 이해가 잘 안 돼요.
examples.en: I listened to all kinds of explanations, but I still don't really get it.

explain: 이런저런 말을 길게 늘어놓는 모습을 못마땅하게 볼 때 써요. 비슷한 말로 '이러니저러니'가 있고, '말하다', '따지다', '떠들다' 같은 말과 잘 어울려요. 말이 많은 사람이나 소문 이야기에 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: People say this and that, but the result is what matters.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뜻이 거의 같고, 말이 많은 상황을 못마땅해하며 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Nearly the same meaning, used when disapproving of all the talk.

phrases.en: People talk this and that about the matter.
phrases.nuance_ko: 남의 일을 두고 이런저런 말을 하는 모습이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes people commenting on someone else's business.

phrases.en: Don't gossip about this and that behind my back.
phrases.nuance_ko: '떠들다'와 함께 쓰면 시끄럽게 소문을 퍼뜨리는 느낌이 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: With '떠들다' it suggests noisily spreading gossip.
phrases.en_equiv: to chatter on about this and that

explain_en: It is used when you find it annoying that someone goes on saying one thing and another. A similar word is '이러니저러니', and it goes well with verbs like '말하다', '따지다' and '떠들다'. It often comes up when talking about chatty people or rumors.

t90.ax: Stop making excuses and apologize first.

en: to talk this and that; to make various remarks

examples.en: Don't gossip about other people's business.

examples.ko: 뒤에서 이러쿵저러쿵해도 저는 신경 안 써요.
examples.en: Even if they talk about me behind my back, I don't care.
Those people go on and on whenever they get together.

examples.ko: 이러쿵저러쿵하는 소리가 듣기 싫어서 자리를 떴어요.
examples.en: I didn't want to hear the grumbling, so I left.
My friend had a lot to say about my choice.
Instead of grumbling, let's finish the work first.

explain: 직접 도와주지는 않으면서 이것저것 평가하고 불평하는 모습에 써요. 말하는 사람이 그런 행동을 달갑게 보지 않는다는 느낌이 들어요. '~을/를 이러쿵저러쿵하다'나 '~에 대해 이러쿵저러쿵하다'로 써요.

phrases.en: The people who grumble about everything don't actually help.
phrases.nuance_ko: 동사를 꾸미는 모양으로, 불평만 하는 사람을 가리킬 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The modifier form, for someone who only complains.
phrases.en_equiv: someone who criticizes this and that

phrases.en: My friends said this and that about my decision.
phrases.nuance_ko: 과거형으로 남이 평가하고 불평했던 일을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Past tense for when others judged or complained.

phrases.en: Stop grumbling and try it yourself.
phrases.nuance_ko: 불평 대신 행동하라고 말할 때 쓰는 연결형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A connective form telling someone to act instead of complaining.

explain_en: It describes someone judging and complaining about this and that without actually helping. The speaker usually finds that behavior unwelcome. Use it as '~을/를 이러쿵저러쿵하다' or '~에 대해 이러쿵저러쿵하다'.

t90.ax: Don't gossip about other people's business.

examples.en: I volunteered to run the event.

examples.ko: 먼저 자원하는 사람이 없어서 제가 손을 들었어요.
examples.en: Nobody volunteered first, so I raised my hand.
The teacher gave points to the student who volunteered to clean.
Who wants to volunteer for tomorrow's presentation?
I was surprised because my younger brother offered to do the dishes.
He volunteers even for dangerous jobs.

explain: '자원하다'는 시키지 않았는데 스스로 나서서 맡겠다고 하는 거예요. 회의나 수업에서 하나를 맡을 때는 '내가 할게요', '지원할게요'라고 더 자주 말해요. 이 단어는 글이나 공식 자리에서 더 자연스러워요. '자원봉사'는 이 말이 들어간 다른 단어예요.

phrases.en: I volunteered to take on the cleaning.
phrases.nuance_ko: 스스로 나서서 일을 맡았다고 할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when someone steps forward to take on a task on their own.

phrases.en: Those who want to volunteer, please raise your hand.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뒤에 명사를 붙여서 '나서는 사람'을 가리킬 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Modifies a noun to refer to people who step forward.

phrases.en: I do volunteer work at the library every weekend.
phrases.nuance_ko: 스스로 나서서 돕는 일을 가리키는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common compound for helping others of one's own free will.

explain_en: Neutral, common — step forward to serve or join an effort. It means stepping forward on your own to take something on without being told. In class or meetings people more often say '내가 할게요' or '지원할게요'. 자원하다 sounds more natural in writing and formal settings. '자원봉사' (volunteer work) is a separate word that contains it.

t90.ax: I volunteered to run the event.

examples.en: He walked off, mumbling something to himself.

examples.ko: 뭘 그렇게 주절거려요? 잘 안 들려요.
examples.en: What are you muttering on about? I can't hear you well.
My friend rambled on the phone for a long time.
The child began babbling before falling asleep.

examples.ko: 혼자 주절거리지 말고 크게 말해 주세요.
examples.en: Don't mutter to yourself. Please say it out loud.
Grandpa keeps muttering away while watching TV.

explain: 낮은 목소리로 알아듣기 어렵게 말을 길게 늘어놓는 모습이에요. '중얼거리다'는 작게 혼잣말하는 느낌이 중심이고, '주절거리다'는 쓸데없는 말을 쭉 이어 가는 느낌이 더 있어요. 조금 가볍거나 못마땅한 말투예요.

phrases.en: He kept on talking and talking.
phrases.nuance_ko: 말이 길게 이어지는 모습을 흉내 낸 말로, 동사 앞에 붙여 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A mimetic adverb for talk that goes on and on, placed before a verb.

phrases.en: The child is mumbling something alone.
phrases.nuance_ko: 작게 혼잣말하는 느낌이 더 중심이고, 못마땅한 느낌은 덜해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Focuses more on quiet muttering to oneself, with less of a disapproving tone.

phrases.example: 옆에서 주절거리지 마세요. 집중이 안 돼요.
phrases.en: Please don't mumble next to me. I can't concentrate.
phrases.nuance_ko: 쓸데없는 말을 그만하라고 할 때 쓰지만 조금 강하게 들릴 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to tell someone to stop babbling, but it can sound a bit harsh.

explain_en: It describes going on at length in a low, hard-to-catch voice. '중얼거리다' centers on quiet self-talk, while '주절거리다' adds the feel of a stream of aimless words. The tone is a bit casual or disapproving.

t90.ax: He walked off, mumbling something to himself.

en: to invent; to fabricate; to make up

examples.en: They say someone made that story up.
The child makes up funny stories.
Don't make up lies.
I made up a reason for being late and told it.
Don't try so hard to come up with an excuse.
Even though it was an invented story, it sounded real.

explain: 없던 이야기나 거짓말을 만들 때 많이 써서 '거짓말, 변명, 이야기'와 잘 어울려요. 소설가가 이야기를 만드는 것에도 써요. '만들어 내다'보다 사실이 아니라는 느낌이 강해요.

phrases.en: He made up a lie as the reason he was late.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사실이 아닌 말을 일부러 만든다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means deliberately making up something untrue.

phrases.en: I made up an excuse because I hadn't done my homework.
phrases.nuance_ko: 잘못을 숨기려고 이유를 꾸며 낼 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when inventing a reason to hide a fault.

phrases.en: That is not a story I made up.
phrases.nuance_ko: 과거를 꾸미는 형태로 '꾸며 낸 이야기'를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A past modifier for a made-up story.

explain_en: Make up stories or excuses that are not real. It often means making up stories or lies, and goes well with '거짓말', '변명' and '이야기'. It is also used when a novelist creates a story. It carries a stronger sense of 'not true' than '만들어 내다'.

en: to be thrown or stuck in; to be shoved into

examples.ko: 안 쓰는 물건이 창고 구석에 처박혀 있어요.
examples.en: Unused things are stuffed away in a corner of the storeroom.

examples.ko: 차가 도랑에 처박혀서 꺼내는 데 한참 걸렸어요.
examples.en: The car got stuck headfirst in a ditch and it took a long time to pull it out.

examples.ko: 비가 와서 주말 내내 방에 처박혔어요.
examples.en: It rained, so I stayed holed up in my room all weekend.

examples.ko: 집에만 처박혀 있지 말고 좀 나가요.
examples.en: Don't just stay holed up at home; go out a bit.
I found old letters that had been stuffed away in a drawer.

examples.ko: 그렇게 방에만 처박히면 몸에도 안 좋아요.
examples.en: Staying holed up in your room like that is bad for your body too.

explain: '박히다'보다 거칠고 세게 들어가거나 구석에 쑤셔 넣어진 느낌이에요. 사람이 나가지 않고 집에 '처박혀 있다'고 하면 틀어박혀 지낸다는 약간 부정적인 말투예요. 편한 사이에서 쓰는 말이에요.

phrases.en: I stayed holed up at home all weekend.
phrases.nuance_ko: 밖에 나가지 않고 지낼 때 쓰는 약간 부정적인 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A slightly negative way to say you stayed in without going out.
phrases.en_equiv: to be holed up at home

phrases.en: The car slammed into a roadside tree.
phrases.nuance_ko: 세게 부딪혀 들어간 모습을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for something crashing hard into an object.
phrases.en_equiv: to slam into a roadside tree

phrases.example: 안 쓰는 옷을 옷장에 처박아 뒀어요.
phrases.en: I shoved the clothes I don't wear into the closet.
phrases.nuance_ko: '처박히다'의 능동형으로, 물건을 아무렇게나 넣어 둘 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The active counterpart, used for stuffing things away carelessly.

explain_en: It feels rougher and more forceful than '박히다', as if something is shoved in or stuffed into a corner. Saying a person is '처박혀 있다' at home means shut away and not going out, with a slightly negative tone. It suits casual talk.

en: to vomit; to throw up; to bring up

examples.en: I threw up everything I ate yesterday.
The baby drank milk and then spit up a little.

examples.ko: 차를 오래 타서 속이 안 좋아 결국 게웠어요.
examples.en: I rode in the car for a long time, felt sick, and finally threw up.

examples.ko: 속이 울렁거려서 화장실에서 다 게워 냈어요.
examples.en: My stomach was churning, so I threw it all up in the bathroom.
If your stomach hurts, don't force yourself to throw up.

examples.ko: 너무 많이 먹으면 게울 수도 있어요.
examples.en: If you eat too much, you might throw up.

explain: '토하다'와 같은 상황에 쓰지만 '토하다'가 더 일상적이고, '게우다'는 먹은 것을 입으로 도로 내보낸다는 느낌이 있어요. 'ㅜ'가 '워'로 바뀌어 '게워요, 게웠어요'가 되고, '게워 내다'처럼도 자주 써요.

phrases.en: I threw up from the long car ride.
phrases.nuance_ko: 같은 뜻이지만 일상에서 더 자주 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: It means the same but is used more often in everyday speech.

phrases.en: The baby brought up what it had eaten.
phrases.nuance_ko: 먹은 것을 입으로 도로 내보낸다는 느낌이 더 잘 드러나요.
phrases.nuance_en: It brings out the feel of sending food back out through the mouth.

phrases.example: 너무 많이 먹어서 먹은 것을 게웠어요.
phrases.en: I ate too much and threw up what I had eaten.
phrases.nuance_ko: '게우다'는 먹은 것을 목적어로 써서 말하는 경우가 많아요.
phrases.nuance_en: 게우다 is often used with what was eaten as its object.
phrases.en_equiv: to throw up what one ate

explain_en: It describes the same situation as '토하다', but '토하다' is more common in daily speech, while '게우다' feels like bringing back up what you ate. The stem changes to '게워요/게웠어요', and it is often used as '게워 내다'.

t90.ax: I threw up everything I ate yesterday.

examples.en: A headband is convenient when you exercise.

examples.ko: 딸이 분홍색 머리띠를 사 달라고 했어요.
examples.en: My daughter asked me to buy her a pink headband.
My head hurts because of the headband.
I bought a cute headband at the festival.
With a headband on, my bangs don't fall down.
He tied a white band around his forehead.

explain: '머리띠를 하다'가 가장 자연스럽고 '두르다'도 써요. '머리핀'은 머리카락을 고정하는 작은 물건이고, '머리띠'는 머리 둘레를 감는 것이에요. 시험 응원 때 이마에 두르는 천도 '머리띠'라고 해요.

phrases.en: I wore a headband today.
phrases.nuance_ko: 머리띠를 쓰고 있는 모습을 가장 자연스럽게 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most natural way to say you are wearing a headband.

phrases.en: I tied a headband around my forehead.
phrases.nuance_ko: 머리 둘레를 감을 때 '두르다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: 두르다 is used when wrapping around the head.

phrases.en: I took off my headband when I got home.
phrases.nuance_ko: 머리에 쓴 머리띠를 벗을 때는 '빼다'라고 자연스럽게 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: 빼다 is the natural verb for taking a headband off your head.

explain_en: '머리띠를 하다' is the most natural, and '두르다' also works. A '머리핀' is a small clip that holds hair, while a '머리띠' wraps around the head. The cloth tied on the forehead to cheer for an exam is also a '머리띠'.

examples.en: The child keeps following me, holding on to my waistband.
Grandfather slipped his hand into his waistband.
Don't walk with your hands in your waistband.
My younger brother's pants keep slipping, so he keeps pulling them up.
The water was deep, so I got wet all the way up to my waist.
A few coins fell out of my waistband.

explain: '허리춤'과 거의 같게 쓰지만 바지의 허리 부분을 가리켜요. '바지춤을 올리다', '바지춤에 손을 넣다'처럼 허리를 잡거나 올리는 동작과 자주 같이 나와요.

phrases.en: The child pulled up the waist of his pants and ran off again.
phrases.nuance_ko: 흘러내린 바지를 허리 쪽으로 끌어올리는 동작에 가장 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common collocation for hitching up pants that have slipped down.

phrases.en: It was cold, so I walked with my hands in the waist of my pants.
phrases.nuance_ko: '바지춤'에 '에'가 붙어 손이나 물건을 넣는 장소로 쓰는 모양이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: With the particle '에', it marks the place where you put a hand or an object.
phrases.en_equiv: to put a hand in one's waistband

phrases.en: He carries his keys at his waist.
phrases.nuance_ko: '바지춤'과 거의 같지만 바지뿐 아니라 허리 부분 전체를 가리켜서 더 넓게 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Nearly the same as '바지춤', but it refers to the waist area in general, not only the pants.

explain_en: It is nearly the same as '허리춤' but points to the waist part of pants. It often appears with actions like pulling up the waistband or putting a hand in it, as in '바지춤을 올리다' and '바지춤에 손을 넣다'.

en: to have a safe delivery; to have an easy labor

examples.en: My older sister safely gave birth to a healthy son.
I prayed, hoping for a safe delivery.

examples.ko: 오늘 아침에 친구가 순산해서 병원에 가고 있어요.
examples.en: My friend gave birth safely this morning, so I'm heading to the hospital.
Everyone was happy at the news that she had delivered safely.

examples.ko: 순산하려면 임신 중에 가벼운 운동도 필요하다고 해요.
examples.en: They say light exercise during pregnancy is needed for an easy delivery.
The baby will be here soon. I hope the delivery goes well!

explain: 아기를 큰 문제 없이 낳았다는 뜻이라서 '출산하다'보다 축하하고 걱정해 주는 느낌이 있어요. 임신한 사람에게 '순산하세요'라고 인사하고, 소식을 전할 때는 '순산했어요', 높일 때는 '순산하셨어요'라고 해요.

phrases.en: Your baby is coming soon, right? Have a safe delivery!
phrases.nuance_ko: 임신한 사람에게 건네는 인사말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A greeting said to a pregnant woman.

phrases.en: The whole family prayed for a safe delivery.
phrases.nuance_ko: 아기를 무사히 낳기를 바란다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means hoping the baby is born safely.
phrases.en_equiv: to pray for a safe delivery

phrases.en: My aunt safely gave birth to a baby girl yesterday.
phrases.nuance_ko: 웃어른이나 높일 사람의 출산 소식을 전할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when reporting the birth for someone you should honor.

explain_en: Because it means giving birth without major trouble, it carries a congratulatory, caring tone that '출산하다' lacks. People greet a pregnant woman with '순산하세요', and say '순산했어요' when sharing news, or '순산하셨어요' to be respectful.

en: to be tingling; to be stinging

examples.ko: 겨울 아침 찬 공기를 마시면 코가 싸해요.
examples.en: When I breathe the cold winter morning air, my nose stings.

examples.ko: 매운 겨자를 먹자 코끝이 싸하게 아팠어요.
examples.en: After eating hot mustard, the tip of my nose tingled painfully.
There was a smell of disinfectant and my nose stung.

examples.ko: 그 말을 듣는 순간 가슴이 싸해졌어요.
examples.en: The moment I heard that, my heart sank with a stinging feeling.

examples.ko: 찬바람 때문에 목이 싸할 때는 따뜻한 차를 마셔요.
examples.en: When my throat stings from the cold wind, I drink warm tea.

examples.ko: 속이 싸해서 물을 한 잔 마셨어요.
examples.en: My stomach stung, so I drank a glass of water.

explain: 코, 목, 속, 가슴이 소독약이나 찬 기운, 매운 것 때문에 아린 느낌이에요. '화하다'는 시원하게 퍼지는 느낌이고, '싸하다'는 아리고 쓰린 느낌이 더 있어요. 마음이 서늘하게 아플 때 '가슴이 싸하다'라고도 해요.

phrases.en: I breathed in the cold air and my nose is stinging.
phrases.nuance_ko: '싸하다'와 가장 잘 어울리는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The pairing that goes best with 싸하다.

phrases.en: My chest felt a chill when I heard that.
phrases.nuance_ko: 마음이 서늘하게 아플 때 비유로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used figuratively when the heart aches with a chill.

phrases.en: The smell of disinfectant makes my nose sting.
phrases.nuance_ko: 아리게 아픈 정도를 말할 때 부사형을 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The adverb form describes a sharp, stinging pain.

explain_en: It describes a stinging, sharp feeling in the nose, throat, stomach or chest from disinfectant, cold air or spicy food. '화하다' feels cool and spreading, while '싸하다' has more of a stinging, smarting feel. People also say '가슴이 싸하다' when the heart aches with a chill.

examples.en: I yawned with my mouth wide open.
I split the watermelon in half with a knife.
The drought was long, so the rice paddy ground cracked wide open.
The wet clothes clung tightly to my body.

examples.ko: 어깨가 쩍 벌어진 남자가 문 앞에 서 있었어요.
examples.en: A broad-shouldered man was standing at the door.

examples.ko: 아이가 쩍 소리가 나게 입맛을 다셨어요.
examples.en: The child smacked his lips with a loud sound.

explain: 입이나 틈이 크게 벌어지거나, 붙어 있던 것이 갈라지고 달라붙는 느낌을 나타내요. '쩍 벌어지다, 쩍 갈라지다, 쩍 달라붙다'처럼 정해진 동사와 함께 쓰는 경우가 많아요. 소리를 흉내 낼 때도 써요.

phrases.en: My jaw dropped when I heard the price.
phrases.nuance_ko: 너무 놀라서 말이 안 나올 때 써요. 실제로 입을 벌렸는지와 상관없이 크게 놀랐다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when you are so amazed you cannot speak. It does not need an actual open mouth; it just means you were greatly astonished.

explain_en: It conveys the feel of something opening wide, splitting, or sticking firmly. It usually pairs with set verbs such as '쩍 벌어지다', '쩍 갈라지다' and '쩍 달라붙다'. It can also imitate a smacking sound.

examples.en: After eating a mint candy, my mouth feels cool and minty.

examples.ko: 치약 맛이 너무 화해서 아이가 싫어해요.
examples.en: The toothpaste is so minty that my child doesn't like it.

examples.ko: 파스를 붙이니 처음에는 화하다가 곧 따뜻해졌어요.
examples.en: When I put on the patch it first felt cooling, then soon warm.

examples.ko: 화한 느낌 때문에 껌을 자주 씹어요.
examples.en: I chew gum often because of the cooling sensation.

examples.ko: 박하 향이 화하게 퍼져서 잠이 깼어요.
examples.en: The mint scent spread sharply and woke me up.

examples.ko: 코가 화할 만큼 시원한 바람이 불었어요.
examples.en: A breeze so cool it made my nose tingle blew by.

explain: 박하, 민트, 파스처럼 입, 코, 피부에 시원하게 퍼지는 느낌이에요. '시원하다'보다 감각이 더 구체적이에요. '화(怒)'와 상관없는 말이니 '화해요'를 '화가 나요'로 오해하지 마세요.

phrases.en: When I chew this gum, my mouth feels minty.
phrases.nuance_ko: '화하다'와 가장 잘 어울리는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The pairing that fits 화하다 best.

phrases.en: A cooling sensation comes when I put on a patch.
phrases.nuance_ko: 박하처럼 시원하게 퍼지는 감각을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes a cooling, spreading sensation like mint.

phrases.en: This candy has a minty taste.
phrases.nuance_ko: 맛을 설명할 때 뒤에 '맛'을 붙여 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Attach 맛 (taste) to describe flavor.

explain_en: It describes a cooling sensation spreading through the mouth, nose or skin, as with mint or a medicated patch. It is more specific than '시원하다'. It has nothing to do with '화' (anger), so don't mistake '화해요' for '화가 나요'.
